messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran an extended perf sweep on a100-prod (2h) focusing on attention kernel mix + KV packing. Observed higher throughput with interleaved packing but intermittent p99 spikes and elevated eviction churn.

maria: Quick microbench summary: separate-KV + paged -> 4.2k tok/s, p99 ~78ms. interleaved + paged -> 4.55k tok/s, p99 jumps to ~105ms during long chats (seq=4096). interleaved + fused-pref (when fused chosen) yields ~4.7k tok/s and p99 ~82ms but fused pref only kicks in for seq<1024 in current selector.

maria: Profiler snippet and allocator trace show fragmentation hotspots at page boundaries and lots of small free ranges. Key excerpt:
```
scenario: chat-long-seq (seq=4096)
kernel_trace: FlashFusedV2 -> paged_attention (fallback mid-request)
kv_packing: interleaved
dtype: bf16
allocator: paged-heap
eviction_count: 342 / 1h
mem_frag: ~24% (hotspots at page edges)
kv_stride_bytes: 6144
kv_entry: 48 bytes
pages_per_entry: 3
alloc_alignment: 256
actual_ptr: 0x7f8b2c01a120 (ptr % 128 != 0)
```

ken: That ptr mod mismatch is concerning. Some fused kernels assume 128B alignment for vector loads; misaligned pointers can force slow copies or unaligned loads in paged kernels. Also flipping kernel mid-request can leave mixed-size allocations that don't coalesce well.

chao: Can you paste the selector logs for why it flipped? We might be miscomputing predicted stride when dtype==bf16 (rounding up differently).

maria: Selector excerpt: "predicted_kv_stride=6000 -> rounded_stride=6144; fused_threshold=4096; decision: try fused, then fallback when seq grows -> paged_alloc"

sam: Two things: (1) selector rounding for bf16 may be off by one page, causing alignment differences; (2) allocator evicter is page-granular and doesn't buddy-coalesce freed ranges, so mixed alloc/dealloc patterns fragment.

perf-bot: regression-alert: perf/regressions: p99_latency +34% for chat-long-seq on commit 0f3a9d. CI trace: https://ci.redwood/prof/0f3a9d

maria: Local experiments with quick patches: enforce 128B alignment on paged KV when dtype==bf16 and enable coalescing in the evicter. Results (same model/config):
- separate_kv + paged: 4200 tok/s, p99 78ms, mem_peak 22GB
- interleaved + paged: 4550 tok/s, p99 105ms, mem_peak 20.6GB
- interleaved + fused-prefer: 4700 tok/s, p99 82ms, mem_peak 20.2GB
- interleaved + align128 + coalesce: 4520 tok/s, p99 81ms, evictions -70%, mem_frag ~6%

chao: Proposed mitigations: 1) allocator: enforce align_kv_to=128 when bf16 or fused-kernel-flag. 2) evicter: implement buddy-style coalesce / shadow compact when fragmentation exceeds 15%. 3) selector: avoid mid-request kernel flips; if flip unavoidable, prefer conservative allocation (separate_kv) for that batch and emit telemetry.

chao: Shadow-compact pseudocode:
```
for page in allocated_pages:
  if page.free_fraction > threshold:
    migrate_live_entries(page -> target_page)
    mark page free
atomic_swap_page_table_entries()
```

sam: Also add a selector safety check: if current heap offset cannot satisfy alignment constraints, selector should mark this allocation as incompatible for fused kernels and either choose separate layout or force align padding. Record an event.

maria: ops-bot suggested a canary flags set: --kv-packing=interleaved --align-kv-stride=128 --evict-coalesce=true. Canaries scheduled on a100 group for 6h window.

ops-bot: canary scheduled: id=rv-kv-frag-2026-03-18, start=2026-03-18T04:00:00Z, group=a100-canary

maria: I pushed a draft patch (allocator align + coalesce + selector safety) behind a feature flag and ran microbench harness: /internal/perf/kv_frag_harness. Initial local runs look promising.

ken: LGTM. Please add microbench permutations for seq={512,1024,2048,4096} x dtype={fp16,bf16} and assert evictions drop and p99 stays bounded. Also add a sanity test for allocator invariants (last_free_ts <= last_alloc_ts).

sam: Add a runtime flag to disable mid-request switching too; that will help isolate the root cause if spikes persist.

chao: I'll add extra kv_stride telemetry (pointer_mod histograms) to correlate pointer mod buckets with latency p99 spikes.

maria: If canary is clean we'll roll to prod next week. Landing PR behind flag and will enable canary at 04:00 UTC tomorrow.

perf-bot: note: added follow-up regression job to CI for 48h

maria: Thanks everyone. Pushed traces and raw alloc logs to the perf artifact store. If you want to inspect the largest fragmentation samples look at artifact id=rv/frag/1932109876.

sam: Nice work. Keep the canary monitor on and let's triage any anomaly ASAP. :thumbsup:
